text:
marco: quick thought — i'm leaning toward a sidecar-routing model for internal APIs. reasoning: local decisions (latency), easier per-tenant quotas, and better isolation for experiments. canaries via header or local weight tables. :thinking:
jen: can you expand on quotas? central gateway makes it trivial to have one global quota engine and consistent billing/metrics though. sidecars mean we duplicate logic + risk drift.
sam: agreed with jen on drift. also curious about the contract between service and sidecar — proto or simple http? my vote: protobuf for the control plane and policy payloads, JSON for external clients. small snippet of what i mean for a route descriptor:
```proto
message RouteConfig {
  string route_id = 1;
  repeated string allowed_models = 2;
  map<string, double> rollout_weights = 3; // header or cookie based
}
```
marco: that proto looks fine. the point is sidecar can enforce per-service policies with tiny local cache, and fallback to central control plane if missing. reduces RTT for most requests. also lets services opt into different batching/kv-cache settings per workload.
olivia: UX and observability are big here — if we go sidecar we need a console view that aggregates sidecar decisions into one timeline so SREs/products see "why" a request was routed. rollout controls in console must show per-service % and let ops flip to central override.
jen: the other big risk is rollout correctness. with many sidecars you can end up with inconsistent canaries (different versions, stale configs). we need strong versioning (schema + checksums) and a forced reconciliation loop. I worry about debugging cross-service traces.
marco: totally. plan would be: protobuf signed manifests + sequence numbers, push via control plane, sidecars expose /health + /config_checksum for quick audits. add metric labels: routing.source=sidecar, routing.policy_v=42.
sam: i want to call out telemetry cardinality — if every sidecar adds too many labels we explode metrics. prefer fixed label set: route_id, policy_v, rollout_bucket. keep histograms for latency and counters for fallback events.
olivia: +1 on fixed label set. and rollout UX: console should let you schedule gradual ramps (0 -> 100 over N minutes), pause on error budget triggers, and show a live sample of requests that hit the canary (redacted).
marco: last point — operational failure modes: sidecar down => fallback to central gateway or local degraded path. propose default policy: if sidecar not reachable, upstream falls back to gateway; if gateway overloaded, request fails fast with 503 and tenant quota reason in body. we should document these clearly.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: sidecar-config-service v1.8.2 -> staging at 1826003380 :rocket:
jen: thanks. i'd like a short spike to prototype sidecar checksum reconciliation and a console mock for rollout controls before we pick a single architecture. 30–60% chance i'm still pro-central after the spike but this will surface tradeoffs. :+1:
marco: sounds good. i'll carve out a 2-day spike and share findings in #eng-platform.
